 Learn more Investing.com -- Shares of Once Upon A Farm PBC (NYSE:OFRM) tumbled over 10% in premarket trade Monday, extending a 6% drop from Friday as mounting product safety concerns sparked aggressive selling. The slide accelerated as investors digested the company's decision to initiate a nationwide recall and reformulation of its Tractor Wheels soft-baked bars.

 Pressure had already begun mounting after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued an urgent advisory warning that the toddler snack line poses a potentially fatal choking hazard. According to federal regulators, the product can form a dense, sticky mass when chewed, creating an airway obstruction that standard first-aid measures, including back blows and the Heimlich maneuver, have struggled to clear. 
 Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks » 
 Following the agency's warning and three consumer complaints, Once Upon a Farm moved to pull all flavors, package sizes, and lots from the market. Management acknowledged the gravity of the disruption, stating that the company fell short of customer trust and acted swiftly to withdraw the line alongside federal authorities. 
 The operational footprint of the recall presents an immediate logistical and financial headwind, covering nationwide e-commerce platforms alongside key retailers like Target, Walmart, and Costco. Beyond the immediate inventory write-offs and refund costs, Wall Street is assessing the broader threat to retail shelf allocations and brand premium in a category defined by strict parental trust. 
 For Once Upon a Farm, containing the fallout will hinge on the speed of its reformulation and its ability to shield the rest of its portfolio from reputational damage. Investors are likely to watch upcoming regulatory updates closely for signs of additional compliance costs or long-term demand erosion.
